punchline: Over the same 25 years the index made 12.5 percent a year and the average fund investor made 7.3.
thirty_sec: Bogle compares 1980 to 2005. The S&P 500 averaged 12.5 percent a year, the average fund investor 7.3. Costs explain only part of the gap. The main cause is behavior: buying funds after a strong stretch, selling after a weak one, and choosing which fund to hold. Bogle's chapter title for it is The Grand Illusion.
